final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful but not curative. The admissible evidence still shows a material limitation affecting a named segment in two agency grant commitments, an unresolved 1.3 percentage-point evaluation gap, an open legal question on disclosure, and a policy requiring such limitations to be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The Actor expressly concedes there is no evidence of remediation, disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or final legal determination. That means the caveat is not merely descriptive wording around an otherwise satisfied policy condition; it is the unresolved compliance condition itself. Aggregate readiness passing, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public guidance on model cards and monitoring may support launch-risk context, but they do not establish policy compliance for certification on the present record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the 1.3 percentage-point gap for the named grant-commitment segment was remediated before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the material limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the named launch use case before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so the policy predicate for certification is unresolved.
The affected segment is named in two agency grant commitments, so the 5% traffic estimate does not negate materiality under the stated policy.
Public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring supports control practices but does not satisfy the internal release-policy requirement for a material named use case.
